related_questions.question: What is the failure rate of Rezum?

text_blocks.snippet: The Rezum procedure for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) has a low failure rate, with studies reporting a surgical reintervention rate of around 4-5% within 5 years. While most patients experience symptom improvement, a small percentage may require additional procedures or medication.

list.title: Low Re-treatment Rate:
list.snippet: Studies indicate that the Rezum procedure boasts a low re-treatment rate. For example, one study reported a 4.4% five-year treatment recurrence rate. Another study showed that less than 5% of patients needed additional procedures or surgeries within five years.

list.title: TOV Failure:
list.snippet: A "Trial Without Catheter" (TOV) failure rate of around 12.1% has also been reported, meaning some patients may require a catheter for a period after the procedure.

list.title: Factors Affecting Success:
list.snippet: A high postvoid residual (PVR) (the amount of urine left in the bladder after urination) is a risk factor for TOV failure.

list.title: Symptom Improvement:
list.snippet: Rezum is generally effective in reducing lower urinary tract symptoms, with studies showing significant improvements in symptom scores and maximum flow rate.

list.title: Durability:
list.snippet: The benefits of Rezum can be durable, with symptom relief and flow rate improvements lasting for at least five years in many patients.

list.title: Compared to other treatments:
list.snippet: Rezum has a lower surgical reintervention rate compared to other minimally invasive procedures like UroLift.
